comment: Ep73 Algeria vs Austria (Group J) — 'The Battle of the Midfields / The Reckoning'. CANON content/Stories/Algeria-vs-Austria.md: a taut midfield duel decided by WILL, climax = the 73rd-minute Mahrez left-foot curl toward the top corner DEFLECTED WIDE by Alaba's outstretched leg (NO goal); ending deliberately unresolved ('separated by a single deflection', 'who blinks first'). OUR PREDICTION = Algeria 0-0 Austria (canon-faithful; the deflection is the peak, no goals). lines.text: Some wounds the football world buries. This one waited forty-four years. Gijón, nineteen eighty-two — the night two European giants shook hands on a scoreline, and sent a brilliant Algeria home. The desert never forgot.
Tonight the Desert Foxes return — to face Austria, one half of that old arrangement. Beneath the Tassili rock, where the Sahara hides paintings twelve thousand years old, an ancient patience stirs.
Welcome back to WorldCup twenty-six Legends — episode seventy-three. Algeria, versus Austria. Group J. The Battle of the Midfields.
Two nations of burning ambition — one forged in mountain snow, one in desert heat. And high in the Alps, they still whisper of the Krampus: the horned shadow that comes for those who grow complacent.
Algeria — the Desert Foxes. Green and white, carrying the dreams of North Africa's most passionate footballing nation.
Riyad Mahrez, the captain — that left foot still bending the impossible. Ismaël Bennacer, the metronome. Amine Gouiri, the spearhead who finishes what they start.
Hicham Boudaoui runs until the grass gives up — and Aïssa Mandi marshals the line that has to hold.
Austria — the Alpine warriors. Tactical, relentless, remade from also-rans into genuine contenders.
David Alaba, the Austrian Messi — Real Madrid's captain, reading the game a beat early. Marcel Sabitzer, the Engine, a thunderbolt in his boot. Konrad Laimer, who treats fatigue as an insult.
Marko Arnautović, the veteran talisman who bends a back four to his will. And Christoph Baumgartner, ghosting late into the box.
So here is the riddle. This match won't be settled by tactics or formations — but by which midfield warrior refuses, in the decisive moment, to blink first.
And before that moment comes — stay with me. Because the seventy-third minute is where the breath stops.
Here is how we see it. A taut, fearless night — darbuka against Alpine drum, two engines running hot, neither giving an inch.
Bennacer glides past the press. Sabitzer winds up from range — and the keeper flies to claw it away.
Then the seventy-third minute arrives. Bennacer receives under pressure from Laimer, and turns with the grace of a man who has done it ten thousand times.
He slides a pass through a gap only he can see. Mahrez is onto it, cutting in from the right — the stadium rises as one — the curl bends toward the top corner.
And Alaba, reading it like a book, stretches out a leg — and deflects it wide. Two masters, one moment. A held breath — and no goal.
This is what the World Cup is for. Not the famous names — the burning ones. Two nations who have always believed they were bigger than their history.
Separated by a single deflection — the desert and the Alps, circling one question: who, in the ninetieth minute, simply wants it more?
Our prediction — Algeria nil, Austria nil. A stalemate forged in fire, where no one's nerve breaks. Not played yet — the real ninety is yours to watch.
Forty-four years on, there is no handshake to send the Foxes home. Only the will of two midfields — and a deflection that kept the answer hidden.
Tonight, neither warrior blinked. And the old wound of Gijón finally met its reckoning, out on the grass.
So you tell me — who wanted it more? Comment ALGERIA for the Desert Foxes — comment AUSTRIA for the Alpine warriors.

High in the Alps, when the nights grow long, the Krampus walks — the horned keeper of the old reckoning, who comes for the complacent and spares only the worthy. It does not forget a debt. Legend seventy-three — the Krampus of the Alps.
The players write the battle. The Krampus carries one truth — every reckoning, however long delayed, arrives. The patient are never truly beaten.
Here is how. Go to worldcup twenty-six dot world and create your free account — ten seconds, and the Krampus, Legend seventy-three, unlocks the moment you sign up.
Then pick three of the forty-eight nations, and every goal they score, scores for you. Free to play, just for fun. No prizes — only glory.
